questions.q: Aerial metagenomics best refers to which one of the following situations?
options: Collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat at one go
Understanding the genetic makeup of avian species of a habitat
Using airborne devices to collect blood samples from moving animals
Sending drones to inaccessible areas to collect plant and animal samples from land surfaces and water bodies
questions.explain: Aerial metagenomics involves collecting DNA samples from the air to study the genetic diversity of microorganisms and other species in a habitat. This technique allows for comprehensive biodiversity assessments. Hence, it refers to collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat at one go.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: Microsatellite DNA' is used in the case of which one of the following?
options: Studying the evolutionary relationships among various species of fauna
Stimulating 'stem cells' to transform into diverse functional tissues
Promoting clonal propagation of horticultural plants
Assessing the efficacy of drugs by conducting series of drug trials in a population
questions.explain: Microsatellite DNA is used to study the evolutionary relationships among species. These short, repetitive sequences of DNA are highly variable and are useful for analyzing genetic diversity and evolutionary patterns. Hence, microsatellite DNA is used in evolutionary studies.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
In the context of vaccines manufactured to prevent COVID-19 pandemic, consider the following statements :
1. The Serum Institute of India produced COVID-19 vaccine named Covishield using mRNA platform.
2. Sputnik V vaccine is manufactured using a vector based platform.
3. COVAXIN is an inactivated pathogen based vaccine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is incorrect: India has majorly relied on the viral vector vaccine Covishield for its vaccination drive. Over 88% of the doses given out so far have been of Covishield, the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine manufactured locally under licence by the Serum Institute of India. Unlike mRNA vaccines, Serum Institutes Covishield uses the viral vector platform.\nStatement 2 is correct: The Sputnik V vaccine is based on a proven well-studied human adenovirus vector platform.\nStatement 3 is correct: Covaxin is an inactivated vaccine. This destroys the pathogen's ability to replicate but keeps it intact so that the immune system can still recognise it and produce an immune response.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best describes the role of B cells and T cells in the human body?
options: They protect the body from environmental allergens.
They alleviate the body's pain and inflammation.
They act as immunosuppressants in the body.
They protect the body from diseases caused by pathogens.
questions.explain: T cells and B cells are part of a specialized network of immune cells that specifically respond to pathogens and fight off infections. B cells and T cells are the white blood cells of the immune system that are responsible for adaptive immune response in an organism. Both the cells are made in the bone marrow. B cells mature in the bone marrow while the T cells travel to the thymus and mature there. These cells are structurally similar and are involved in adaptive immune response in an organism
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Consider the following statements :
DNA Barcoding can be a tool to :
1. assess the age of a plant or animal.
2. distinguish among species that look alike.
3. identify undesirable animal or plant materials in processed foods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explain: DNA barcoding is a method of identifying biological specimens and distinguishing among species that look alike. It involves sequencing of stretches of the genomic region which evolves fast enough to allow species-level discrimination.\nStatement 1 is incorrect: To measure the age of plant and animal remains from the more recent past, scientists use a radioactive isotope of carbon, called carbon-14, as their clock.\nStatements 2 and 3 are correct: DNA Barcoding can be used to distinguish among species that look alike and identify the undesirable animal or plant materials in processed foods. DNA barcoding in plants not only speeds up writing the encyclopedia of life, but also opens up the possibility of establishing a Digital Plant Identification System (DPIS) which works independently of type, age, or developmental stage of the sample under study. Hence, if used properly, DNA barcoding can be an effective and efficient tool for exploring and protecting biodiversity, expediting bioprospecting, and defending against bio-piracy.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Consider the following statements :
1. Biofilms can form on medical implants within human tissues.
2. Biofilms can form on food and food processing surfaces.
3. Biofilms can exhibit antibiotic resistance.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.explain: Biofilm is a complex structure of microbiome having different bacterial colonies or single types of cells in a group; that adhere to the surface.\nStatements 1 & 2 are correct: Biofilms can be formed on medical implants with human tissues, food, and food processing surfaces. Hence, they pose grave health issues, especially in the form of infections.\nStatement 3 is correct: Bacterial biofilms are a serious global health concern due to their ability to tolerate antibiotics (exhibiting antibiotic resistance), host defence systems and other external stresses; therefore it contributes to persistent chronic infections.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
With reference to recent developments regarding 'Recombinant Vector Vaccines', consider the following statements:
1. Genetic engineering is applied in the development of these vaccines.
2. Bacteria and viruses are used as vectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is correct: Recombinant vector vaccines are live replicating viruses that are engineered to carry extra genes derived from a pathogen like Bacteria and viruses. These extra genes produce proteins against which we want to generate immunity. These vaccine genomes may evolve to lose the extra genes during the process of manufacture of the vaccine or replication within an individual, and there is a concern that this evolution might severely limit the vaccine's efficacy.\nStatement 1 is correct: As a result of advances in the fields of molecular biology and genetic engineering, it is now possible to create live recombinant vectors capable of delivering heterologous antigens by the introduction of antigen-encoding genes.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
In the context of hereditary diseases, consider the following statements:
1. Passing on mitochondrial diseases from parent to child can be prevented by mitochondrial replacement therapy either before or after in vitro fertilization of the egg.
2. A child inherits mitochondrial diseases entirely from mother and not from father.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Mitochondrial disease, or mitochondrial disorder, refers to a group of disorders that affect the mitochondria, which are tiny compartments that are present in almost every cell of the body.\nStatement 2 is correct: An individual's mitochondrial genome is entirely derived from the mother because sperm contain relatively few mitochondria, and these are degraded after fertilization. It follows that mitochondrial inheritance is essentially maternal inheritance. It is observed that a child inherits mitochondrial diseases entirely from the mother and not from the father.\nStatement 1 is correct: Mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT) is a new form of reproductive in vitro fertilization (IVF) which works on the principle of replacing a woman's abnormal mitochondrial DNA (mt-DNA) with the donor's healthy one. Passing on mitochondrial diseases from parent to child can be prevented by mitochondrial replacement therapy either before or after in vitro fertilization of an egg.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Bacteria
2. Fungi
3. Virus
Which of the above can be cultured in artificial/synthetic medium?
questions.explain:
Bacteria can be formed in simple, synthetic or complex media, where they vary in nutritional make-up.
- Simple media facilitates the growth of non-fastidious bacteria, and the exact chemical compositions of simple media are known.
- Synthetic media is composed of minimal ingredients needed for the growth of microorganisms, for example, Davis and Mingioli Medium.
- In complex media, the exact chemical composition is not known, for example, in Tryptic Soy Broth.
Fungal Media containing high carbohydrate sources and nitrogen sources are required for the growth of fungi at a pH range of 5 to 6 and a temperature range from 15 to 37˚C. There are two general types of fungal culture media: natural and synthetic. Natural media are composed of natural substrates, such as herbaceous or woody stems, seeds, leaves, corn meal, wheat germ, oatmeal, etc.
Cultivation of Viruses: Viruses cannot be cultured in an artificial/synthetic medium. Viruses require a living host cell for replication.

questions.q: The term 'ACE2' is talked about in the context of
options: genes introduced in the genetically modified plants
development of India's own satellite navigation system
questions.explain: A coronavirus is surrounded by a fatty outer layer (envelope) and on the surface of this layer is the corona (crown) of spikes made of protein. On the surface of human cells is an enzyme called angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), which acts as the receptor that enables SARS-CoV2 to launch its attack. The virus's spike protein binds to the receptor, then fuses with the cell surface, and releases its genetic material (RNA in the case of SARS-CoV2) into the cell. The coronavirus that causes SARS, called SARS-CoV, uses the same ACE2 receptor to invade a cell. Once inside, the virus replicates itself by using the cell's molecular mechanism. All these stages involve various interactions between virus proteins and human proteins. Any treatment being developed or researched will look to inhibit these activities at one stage or the other.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Consider the following statements :
1. Adenoviruses have single-stranded DNA genomes whereas retroviruses have double-stranded DNA genomes.
2. Common cold is sometimes caused by an adenovirus whereas AIDS is caused by a retrovirus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Adenoviruses contain a double-stranded DNA genome. Retroviruses contain RNA genome. Adenoviruses are common viruses that typically cause the common cold - or flu-like illness. HIV which causes AIDS is a retrovirus.

questions.explain: Bollgard I Bt cotton (single-gene technology) and Bollgard II (double-gene technology) are genetically modified cotton varieties approved for commercialization in India. They provide in-built protection against bollworm infestations using genes from Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt).

questions.q:
What is the importance of using Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines in India?
1. These vaccines are effective against pneumonia as well as meningitis and sepsis.
2. Dependence on antibiotics that are not effective against drug-resistant bacteria can be reduced.
3. These vaccines have no side effects and cause no allergic reactions.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines are effective against pneumonia, meningitis and sepsis. Their use can reduce dependence on antibiotics that are ineffective against drug-resistant bacteria. However, these vaccines can have side effects like fever and loss of appetite.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements :
1. Genetic changes can be introduced in the cells that produce eggs or sperms of a prospective parent.
2. A person's genome can be edited before birth at the early embryonic stage.
3. Human induced pluripotent stem cells can be injected into the embryo of a pig.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: All three statements are correct. Genetic changes can be introduced in gamete-producing cells. Genome editing is possible at the early embryonic stage. Human induced pluripotent stem cells have been successfully injected into pig embryos.

questions.q: In the context of recent advances in human reproductive technology, 'Pronuclear Transfer' is used for
options: Fertilization of egg in vitro by the donor sperm
Genetic modification of sperm producing cells
Development of stem cells into functional embryos
Prevention of mitochondrial diseases in offspring
questions.explain: Pronuclear Transfer involves transferring pronuclei from one zygote to another. It has the potential to prevent mitochondrial diseases in offspring as mitochondrial DNA is transmitted maternally.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: What is the Cas9 protein that is often mentioned in the news?
options: A molecular scissors used in targeted gene editing.
A biosensor used in the accurate detection of pathogens in patients.
A gene that makes plants pest-resistant.
A herbicidal substance synthesized in generally modified crops.
questions.explain: Cas9 is an enzyme that acts as molecular scissors to cut DNA at a specific location as part of the CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing tool. It allows scientists to modify gene sequences by cutting DNA and then letting natural DNA repair processes take over.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
RNA interference (RNAi) technology has gained popularity in the last few years. Why?
1. It is used in developing gene silencing therapies.
2. It can be used in developing therapies for the treatment of cancer.
3. It can be used to develop hormone replacement therapies.
4. It can be used to produce crop plants that are resistant to virtual pathogens.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: RNA interference is used in developing gene silencing therapies, cancer treatments, and producing pathogen-resistant crops. It is not used to develop hormone replacement therapies.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: With reference to the recent developments in science, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Functional chromosomes can be created by joining segments of DNA taken from cells of different species.
Pieces of artificial functional DNA can be created in laboratories.
A piece of DNA taken out from an animal cell can be made to replicate outside a living cell in a laboratory.
Cells taken out from plants and animals can be made to undergo cell division in laboratory petri dishes.
questions.explain: It is not possible to create functional chromosomes by joining DNA segments from different species. Chromosomes are very long and code for many genes. Within a species, translocation can occur, but joining chromosomes from different species does not produce functional chromosomes.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
With reference to the Genetically Modified mustard (GM mustard) developed in India, consider the following statements:
1. GM mustard has the genes of a soil bacterium that give the plant the property of pest-resistance to a wide variety of pests.
2. GM mustard has the genes that allow the plant cross-pollination and hybridization.
3. GM mustard has been developed jointly by the IARI and Punjab Agricultural University.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: GM mustard (DMH-11) contains genes from soil bacteria, but these do not confer pest resistance. It does have genes allowing cross-pollination and hybridization. It was developed by Delhi University scientists, not IARI and Punjab Agricultural University.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: What is the application of Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer Technology?
options: Production of organisms free of diseases
questions.explain: Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer (SCNT) is a technology used in cloning, stem cell research, and regenerative medicine. It involves transferring the nucleus of a somatic cell into an enucleated egg cell. This technique is used for reproductive cloning of animals, as demonstrated by the cloning of Dolly the sheep in 1997.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
With reference to agriculture in India, how can the technique of 'genome sequencing', often seen in the news, be used in the immediate future? (2017)
1. Genome sequencing can be used to identify genetic markers for disease resistance and drought tolerance in various crop plants.
2. This technique helps in reducing the time required to develop new varieties of crop plants.
3. It can be used to decipher the host-pathogen relationships in crops.
questions.explain:
Genome sequencing is the process of determining the complete DNA sequence of an organism's genome. It involves figuring out the order of DNA nucleotides, or bases, in a genome—the order of As, Cs, Gs, and Ts that make up an organism's DNA.

Statement 1 and statement 2 are correct: Genomes for plant diseases allow the detection of rare disorders that can be prevented or better treated by early detection and intervention. Genome sequencing is also now used in farming adding speed and precision to selective breeding methods. It is also being used in farming various crop plants.

Statement 3 is correct: Genome sequence reveals a compact genome, a dependency of the pathogen on its host for some essential nutrients and a potential role in the regulation of host plant cytokinin and auxin.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: In the context of the developments in Bioinformatics, the term 'transcriptome', sometimes seen in the news, refers to (2016)
options: A range of enzymes used in genome editing
The full range of mRNA molecules expressed by an organism
The description of the mechanism of gene expression
A mechanism of genetic mutations taking place in cells
questions.explain: Transcriptome is the sum total of all the messenger RNA molecules expressed from the genes of an organism. It is the full range of messenger RNA, or mRNA, molecules expressed by an organism. The term transcriptome can also be used to describe the array of mRNA transcripts produced in a particular cell or tissue type. In contrast with the genome, which is characterised by its stability, the transcriptome actively changes. In fact, an organism's transcriptome varies depending on many factors, including the stage of development and environmental conditions.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Consider the following techniques/phenomena: (2014)
1. Budding and grafting in fruit plants
2. Cytoplasmic male sterility
3. Gene silencing
Which of the above is/are used to create transgenic crops?
questions.explain:
Transgenic plants are the ones whose DNA is modified using genetic engineering techniques. The aim is to introduce a new trait to the plant which does not occur naturally in the species. Cytoplasmic male sterility and gene silencing technique is used to create transgenic crops.

Cytoplasmic male sterility is total or partial male sterility in plants. These systems are widely exploited in crop plants for hybrid breeding due to the convenience of controlling sterility.

Gene silencing using RNA interference technology, transcriptional gene silencing, and virus-induced gene silencing, is commonly used in horticulture crops. The presence of double-stranded RNA inside the cell leads to the production of small interfering RNAs, short hairpin RNAs and microRNAs.

Grafting and budding are horticulture techniques used to join parts from two or more plans so that they appear to grow as a single plant. In grafting the upper part of one plant grows on the root system of another plant. In the budding process, a bud is taken from one plant and grown on another. It does not lead to any genetic modification.

questions.q:
Mycorrhizal biotechnology has been used in rehabilitating degraded sites because mycorrhiza enables the plants to (2013)
1. Resist drought and increase the absorptive area
2. Tolerate extremes of pH
3. Resist disease infestation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
Mycorrhizal is a fungus which grows in association with the roots of a plant in a symbiotic or mildly pathogenic relationship. These specialised fungi colonise plant roots and extend far into the soil.

Statement 1 is correct: Mycorrhizal root systems increase the absorbing area of roots 10 to 1000 times, thereby greatly improving the ability of the plants to utilise the soil resource.

Statement 2 is correct: Mycorrhizal plants occur in all terrestrial environments where their host plants grow. This includes soils with varying pH from as low as 3 to as high as 9.5 (extremes of pH).

Statement 3 is correct: Mycorrhizal fungi provide an effective alternative method of disease control, especially for those pathogens which affect below-ground plant organs.

questions.q:
Recombinant DNA technology (Genetic Engineering) allows genes to be transferred (2013)
1. across different species of plants
2. from animals to plants
3. from microorganisms to higher organisms
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
Recombinant DNA technology combines DNA from different sources to create a different sequence of DNA. Recombinant DNA technology is the joining of DNA molecules from two different species.

Statement 1 is correct: Recombinant DNA technology combines DNA from different sources to create a different sequence of DNA.

Statement 2 is correct: Recombinant DNA technology has been used in Vaccines Creation where viral proteins are produced by bacteria or yeast from recombined viral genes.

Statement 3 is correct: Recombinant DNA technology has been used to produce both insect and herbicide-resistant crops.

questions.q:
Other than resistance to pests, what are the prospects for which genetically engineered plants have been created? (2012)
1. To enable them to withstand drought
2. To increase the nutritive value of the produce
3. To enable them to grow and do photosynthesis in spaceships and space stations
4. To increase their shelf life.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Genetically engineered plant (GE plant) means a plant in which the genetic material has been changed through in vitronucleic acid techniques, including recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and direct injection of nucleic acid into cells or organelles. Also referred to as a genetically modified (GM) or recombinant DNA (rDNA) or transgenic plant.\n\nGenetically modified (GM) or transgenic plants, have been and are being developed with the aim of enhancing productivity; decreasing dependence on the use of agricultural chemicals; and improving the nutritional value of foods and livestock feeds, longer shelf life, increase resistance to droughts, increase resistance to insects, pests, increased resistance to herbicides.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
With reference to 'stem cells', frequently in the news, which of the following statements is/are correct? (2012)
1. Stem cells can be derived from mammals only.
2. Stem cells can be used for screening new drugs.
3. Stem cells can be used for medical therapies.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
Stem cells are special human cells that are able to develop into many different cell types. This can range from muscle cells to brain cells. In some cases, they can also fix damaged tissues.

Statement 1 is not correct: Stem cells can be derived from two main sources: adult body tissues and embryos. Scientists are also working on techniques to develop stem cells from other cells, using genetic reprogramming techniques.

Statement 2 is correct: Scientists use stem cells in laboratories to test new drugs for safety and effectiveness before they are tested on humans. Scientists can also test how drugs might affect different organs such as the heart or the liver by programming stem cells to acquire properties of the organ the drugs are targeting.

Statement 3 is correct: It can also be used to understand how disease occurs by studying how stem cells turn into specific tissue such as heart muscles or nerves.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
What are the reasons for the people's resistance to the introduction of BT brinjal in India? (2012)
1. Bt brinjal has been created by inserting a gene from a soil fungus into its genome.
2. The seeds of Bt brinjal are terminator seeds and therefore, the farmers have to buy the seeds before every season from the seed companies.
3. There is an apprehension that the consumption of Bt brinjal may have adverse impact on health.
4. There is some concern that the introduction of BT brinjal may have adverse effect on the biodiversity.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is not correct: Bt Brinjal is a transgenic brinjal created by inserting a gene cry1Ac from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis into Brinjal.

Statement 2 is not correct: The seeds of Bt brinjal are not terminator seeds. Although proposed nearly 20 years ago, so-called 'terminator' seeds have never been developed and do not currently exist. Seeds from Bt brinjal open-pollinated varieties will be free for farmers to save and replant as they wish.

Statement 3 is correct: An independent inquiry has revealed that the cultivation of genetically engineered (GE, also called genetically modified, or GM) Bt brinjal poses risks to the environment and possibly to human health.

Statement 4 is correct: Genetically engineered Bt brinjal has several implications on plant biodiversity. An independent study commissioned by Greenpeace International finds that brinjal relatives do occur in the regions where cultivation of GE Bt brinjal is proposed and that GE Bt brinjal may mate with these relatives to spread the GE Bt gene.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
At present, scientists can determine the arrangement or relative positions of genes or DNA sequences on a chromosome. How does this knowledge benefit us? (2011)
1. It is possible to know the pedigree of livestock.
2. It is possible to understand the causes of all human diseases.
3. It is possible to develop disease-resistant animal breeds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain:
DNA sequencing has various applications:

DNA sequencing in Evolutionary biology: The ability to sequence the whole genome of many related organisms has allowed large-scale comparative genomics, and phylogenetics to know the pedigree of livestock and evolutionary studies. (Statement 1 is correct)

DNA sequencing in Diagnostics and Medicine: DNA sequencing has applications in screening the risk of genetic diseases, gene therapy-based treatments, genetic engineering, and gene manipulation. However, it cannot be claimed that it is possible to understand the causes of all human diseases. (Statement 2 is not correct)

DNA sequencing in Agriculture: Sequencing microorganisms to engineer resistant genes in crops also helps in developing disease-resistant animal breeds, mapping and whole-genome sequencing of food plants to increase productivity and nutritional contents as well as environmental tolerance. (Statement 3 is correct)
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: A genetically engineered form of brinjal, known as the Bt-Brinjal, has been developed. The objective of this is (2011)
options: To improve its taste and nutritive qualities
questions.explain: A genetically engineered form of brinjal gives resistance against insects such as the Brinjal Fruit and Shoot Borer (Leucinodes orbonalis). It was developed by Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds Company (Mahyco). The father of India's Green Revolution, S Swaminathan, had asked for an independent study on the long-term toxicity of Bt Brinjal before approving it for commercial use.\n\nBt. Cotton is the only Genetically Modified (GM) crop approved in 2002 by the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for commercial cultivation in the Country and, therefore, cultivation of other unapproved GM crops are banned in India. Few incidences of suspected open cultivation of Bt. Brinjal and HT cotton were reported in Maharashtra, Haryana, Punjab, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh.
